name: mcdb
tagline: Memory-mapped constant database: a faster, thread-safe, >4 GB rewrite of D. J. Bernstein's cdb.
description: mcdb is a C library for building and reading constant (write-once, read-many) key-value files, derived from Dan Bernstein's cdb. A database is written in one pass and then mmap'd read-only, so a lookup is a hash plus one or two page touches with no locking, and the format removes cdb's 4 GB ceiling and adds thread-safe readers. The package also includes nss_mcdb, which compiles passwd, group, hosts and similar files into mcdb databases as a faster alternative to nscd. The last code change was v0.10 in late 2022; it is finished, working code with a single maintainer rather than a living project.
statusNote: No commits since December 2022 (v0.10); stable and usable but effectively unmaintained.

scale.notes: One immutable file per database; updates mean rebuilding the file and atomically renaming it into place.

strengths: Lookups touch only one or two mmap'd pages with no locking on the read path
Supports databases larger than 4 GB, unlike the original cdb
Thread-safe readers and a simple build-then-rename update model
nss_mcdb serves passwd/group/hosts lookups faster than nscd
weaknesses: Immutable: any change requires rebuilding the whole file
Single maintainer and no commits since 2022
C API (plus a Perl binding) only; no server or network access
useCases: Read-only lookup tables shipped with an application
Fast NSS backends for passwd, group and hosts data
Static routing or configuration maps rebuilt in batch
Studying cdb-style constant hash file formats
